summary: Sungtaek Cho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at Stony Brook University and Korea University, serving as Director at the latter around 2012–2013.
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the doctoral supervision of Phillip Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, Calcutta, London, Sorbonne, and Paris under Jules Bloch. He held posts at Calcutta, Pennsylvania, Sahitya Akademi, and the Government of India.

Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) worked in philosophy and Indology. She studied under Surendranath Dasgupta and earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge before serving as a Reader in philosophy at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervision of Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta and Cambridge under J. M. E. McTaggart and James Ward. His posts included Chittagong College, Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Calcutta.
Surendranath Sen (1890–1962) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1939) and the University of Delhi (~1950–1953).

Surya Kumar Bhuyan (1894–1964) worked in Indology and history, studying at Cotton University, Presidency University, Calcutta, and SOAS. His career included roles at Cotton University, Jorhat Mission School, Nowgong College, and serving as Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957–1958).

Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, also studying with Bernard Faure, D. Max Moerman, Michael Como, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.
Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1971 to 2012.

Susan Naquin is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Stanford and Yale, she served on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1988) and Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served on the faculty in the religion department at Amherst College from around 1978 to 2020.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a scholar of Indology who studied at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard, and Radcliffe. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), was a professor at the University of Chicago (1964), and presided over the APSA (2003–2004).

Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist educated at Presidency College, Calcutta, SOAS, and Bonn. He held positions at Presidency College, Calcutta, Dhaka, Sanskrit College, Jadavpur University, and the University of London.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura. He has held part-time lecturer posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, and Bukkyo University.

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He held major posts at the University of Tokyo (1987–2013) and Sophia University (~2013–2021), among other institutions.
